summary: Move mišoʕiwa to Detransitive Infectum-wa, sense 2 adhesion.
rationale: The overt -wa and edition would bind/stick identify Infectum-wa; rags adhere to legs, unlike a surface being plastered.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Ishaq Material culture/59)

data.turoyo: ŭ bəṯr məd‿šīʕ ṭowo baq+qayse, məd hīw ele u+qaləb di+qəšto baq+qayse damixe dmaḥatte ʕul manək <...>
data.translation: and after it became well-covered by logs, after the shape of an arch was given to it (i.e., the house) with the horizontal logs they put above those ones <...>

rationale: First Detransitive Preterit example; agent omitted, material expressed, preserve exact šīʕ.

summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.12/3214)

data.turoyo: Maḥtiwo maye aʕlayye w marṯəḥiwole kop, kop, kop, kop feme du dasto šiʕo, šayʕiwole b ṭino b lagan mede buwe w maye b feme.
data.translation: They put water over them and brought it to the boil, kop, kop, kop, kop, the cauldron's mouth sealed; they sealed it with clay, with a basin, something with it, and water at its mouth.

rationale: First proposed Detransitive Part. Pass.: sealed mouth contrasted directly with agentive šayʕiwole b ṭino. Masculine nominal -o is possible; reader feminine identification is not secure.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) verputzt, abgedichtet, bedeckt werden
rationale: Patient-oriented counterpart of the established coating/sealing sense; šīʕ with a material complement establishes a Detransitive Preterit in one source.

summary: New sense 2: (Detrans.) anhaften, festkleben (mit b-)
rationale: Make the already quoted rags-adhering-to-legs use explicit; this is adhesion, not the patient-oriented being-plastered sense. No previous Detransitive sense numbers exist.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.2/10)

data.turoyo: U qawro bəṯr məd ṣxərre, kšayʕile b ṭino w tawno w ksaymi aʕle ṣlibo.
data.translation: Wenn sie das Grab geschlossen haben, verputzen sie es mit Lehm und Heu und machen ein Kreuz darauf.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.1; explicit grave theme and b-material clay/straw.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 4.2/9)

data.turoyo: w šayʕina feme du farmo aʕle w ṭər bošəl ṭamo.
data.translation: Dann dichten wir die Tür des Ofens hinter ihm ab, und er soll dort brennen.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.1; opening as object and enclosed person as ʕal-complement.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 4.2/10)

data.turoyo: komər mədde u zʕuraṯṯe mawballe su ḥəmmamči, ǧġərre u ḥəmmam w mḥalaqqe bu farmo di nuro w šəʕʕe fem du tarʕo aʕle, w aṯən ṭralle.
data.translation: Sie nahmen ihren Jungen und brachten ihn zum Bademeister, sie schürten das Bad an und warfen ihn in den Feuerofen. Sie dichteten die Tür des Ofens hinter ihm ab, gingen nach Hause und ließen ihn zurück.

rationale: Thin Preterit I.1; plural assimilated šəʕʕe and same valency as /9.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/62)

data.turoyo: Hən nuqliwa, ŭ hən maḥtiwa hul dmiswewa bu+ṭino. Šayʕíwayle hawxa.
data.translation: Some would bring it, and some would put it until it would get level with clay. They would smooth it out like so.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1; smoothing a clay roof, overt patient suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (MAC Ishaq Material culture/70)

data.turoyo: Ṭabi, hano kowe li+čmənto, lu+šyoʕo dab+bote, lu+bnóyowe.
data.translation: Naturally, this is for the cement, it was for smoothing the houses, for building.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv I.1; patient houses and purpose lu- put the existing isolated form in context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/160)

data.turoyo: N. E, e, hanək ... šan dmolənne hawxa, maḥti rezat d̥kefe ŭ buġre, ŭ bəṯr g̊šayʕiwa hawxa ŭ yətwiwa aʕlayye. Xud uʕdo bdukṯe d̥ani.
data.translation: Yes, yes, those ... in order to fill them like so, they put rows of stones and pebbles, and then they would plaster them like so, and would sit upon them. Like now, instead of these things.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1; stone/pebble seating ledges, preserve the ring over g.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/161)

data.turoyo: Maydínale maḥtínale bu+šuro, ŭ čík̇ənk̇e ha hawxa d̥owe ṣṭān. ŭ šayʕiwa, šayʕíwaynale arʕe, ŭ maḥtíwayna šayʕíwaynale, dək ... saymíwaynale dəkkane hawxa xud̥‿kəmmat, dukṯe du+tāšt, dukṯe di+ṣeniye dam+maye, ŭ mədə‿ǧġəḷḷan, kaməl.
data.translation: We take it, we put it by the wall, so that it is slanted a little bit like so. And they plastered over, we plastered over its bottom, and we would put it and plaster over it, we would make it a dəkkane like you say, a place for a basin, a place for a water bowl, and when we fired it up, it became finished.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1; one quotation includes three source tokens, including 1pl whole-object suffix plus named part arʕe.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (94/246)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr kəzzən, košayʕi ak kurkat b ann adroṯe. Yaʕni tre daste rabe w košəlqi aḥ ḥeṭani, hul towən danoke.
data.translation: Dann verschmiert man die Herde auf den Tennen bzw. baut solche aus mit erde verschmierten Steinen auf, d. h. zwei große Kessel, und siedet den Weizen, bis er gekocht zu (dānōqe geworden) ist.

rationale: Thin Infectum I.1; hearth preparation context, edition’s explanatory material retained without imputing it to an overt Turoyo argument.

summary: Active coating, sealing openings, plastering roofs/hearths and smoothing clay remain one established sense. These are material/object changes, not independent technical senses.
Valency contrasts bare opening/surface objects, suffixal patients, b-material and ʕal-enclosed person. Whole tannoor object suffix with arʕe identifies the treated part.

The existing Detransitive rags example has overt -wa and an adhesion meaning. Its box is corrected to Infectum-wa and its sense made explicit as 2; new Detransitive 1 is the direct coating/sealing counterpart.

PrS 18/22–23 repeats the boat instruction/execution already cited as prs 43/8–9. These page/verse citation systems are not assumed contradictory and no duplicate examples are added. 72/3, /5 and 94/22 are also already cited.
All inherited unnumbered active examples receive sense 1; their text remains unchanged. No collocation requires a new Idiomatic phrases entry.
Round 1 already supplied Detransitive coating/sealing sense 1 and adhesion sense 2. šiʕo at Jan 2.12/3214 supports only the former, not a new sense.
Active Infectum-wa sense 1 already has four examples after round 1. The readers’ repeated thin-cell proposals ignore those additions; no routine Jan active example is added.

The -o of šiʕo does not by itself establish feminine agreement. With masculine feme, a masculine Part. Pass. result predicate is plausible. This new-box proposal remains provisional because a reduced finite Detransitive form or reference to dasto cannot be excluded from the single passage.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
MAC Material culture/59: confirm šīʕ as the Detransitive of coating/sealing when the material is logs rather than plaster. This box currently has one textual context.
Confirm the government in inherited mišoʕiwa appe: the rags adhere to legs; is b- the appropriate dictionary government label?
PrS page/verse correspondence: confirm prs 43/8–9 = PrS 18/22–23 before replacing any citation; no replacement is proposed here.

Confirm šiʕo at Jan 2.12/3214 as a masculine Part. Pass. agreeing with feme; alternatively does it form a finite Detransitive clause with an understood feminine dasto? Verify before treating the proposed box as a settled paradigm.
Patient-oriented covering uses logs rather than coating earth in one Detransitive Preterit; this is a material extension, not a timber-specific sense.
Distillation fittings and wine-jar mouths are coated/sealed as are roofs, boats and openings in round 1; no beverage-specific sense or fixed idiom is established.
